knowledge_units.name: Third-person singular -s/-es
knowledge_units.behavior: Add -s/-es to the main verb in affirmative present-simple statements whose subject is he, she, it or a singular noun.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: Affirmative present-simple main verb, singular third-person subject, no modal or auxiliary before the verb.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The main verb carries -s/-es (or the correct irregular form: has, does, goes).

l1_note.es: En español todas las personas llevan marca verbal; en inglés solo la 3.ª singular, y se omite fácil al producir rápido.

explanation.es: En presente simple, con he/she/it o un sujeto singular, el verbo termina en -s/-es.
explanation.en: In the present simple, a singular third-person subject takes -s/-es on the verb.

knowledge_units.name: “responsible for”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “responsible for” (not of/about/to/in) to express ownership of a task or outcome.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses that someone is accountable for a task, area or outcome using “responsible”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “responsible” is followed by “for” + noun or gerund.
out_of_scope: “responsible to” meaning accountable to a person

l1_note.es: “responsable de” invita a decir “responsible of”.

explanation.es: Se dice “responsible for”, no “responsible of”.
explanation.en: We say “responsible for”, not “responsible of”.

knowledge_units.name: First conditional: present tense in the if-clause
knowledge_units.behavior: In an if-clause about a real future possibility, use the present tense, not will/would.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner states a real, plain future condition with “if”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The if-clause verb is in the present (simple, continuous or perfect), not will/would.
out_of_scope: “if you will” meaning willingness or politeness

l1_note.es: El español usa presente de indicativo tras “si” en estos casos, pero el futuro del resto de la frase arrastra “will” al if-clause.

explanation.es: Tras “if” con una condición futura real se usa presente: “If he approves, we will start.”
explanation.en: After “if” in a real future condition use the present: “If he approves, we will start.”

knowledge_units.name: make / let + object + base verb
knowledge_units.behavior: After active “make” and “let” + object, use the base verb (no “to”, no -ing).
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner uses active make/let with a person or thing as object followed by a verb.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The verb after the object is a bare infinitive.
out_of_scope: passive “be made to + verb” (which is correct)

l1_note.es: “hacer que / dejar que” + subjuntivo empuja a “to” o -ing.

explanation.es: make/let + objeto + verbo base: “made us repeat”, “lets us work”.
explanation.en: make/let + object + base verb: “made us repeat”, “lets us work”.

knowledge_units.name: Choosing the right form of “manage”
knowledge_units.behavior: Choose the word form of the manage family that the sentence slot requires.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: A slot that requires a specific part of speech of the manage family (verb, noun for activity, noun for person, adjective).
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The chosen form matches the required part of speech and meaning.

l1_note.es: Confundir sustantivo de actividad, de persona y adjetivo por cognados (gestión / gerente / manejable).

explanation.es: manage (verbo) · management (actividad) · manager (persona) · manageable (adjetivo).
explanation.en: manage (verb) · management (activity) · manager (person) · manageable (adjective).

knowledge_units.name: “agree” as a verb (no auxiliary 'be')
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “agree” directly as a verb without the auxiliary verb “to be”.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses concurrence or agreement with an idea, proposal, or person using “agree”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “agree” is used as a finite verb with its subject; forms with “am/is/are agree” are absent.

l1_note.es: «Estoy de acuerdo» empuja al calco erróneo «I am agree».

explanation.es: En inglés «agree» ya es un verbo: se dice «I agree», nunca «I am agree».
explanation.en: In English “agree” is already a verb: say “I agree”, never “I am agree”.

knowledge_units.name: “since” vs “for” with duration
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “for” with an extent or duration of time, and “since” only with a specific starting point in time.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner indicates duration or starting point of an action or state continuing into the present.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Durations take “for”; starting points take “since”.

l1_note.es: «Desde hace X años» hace que los hispanohablantes digan «since 3 years» en vez de «for 3 years».

explanation.es: Usa «for» para duración («for two years») y «since» para punto de inicio («since 2021»).
explanation.en: Use “for” for a period of time (“for two years”) and “since” for a starting point (“since 2021”).

knowledge_units.name: “depend on”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “depend on” (not “depend of”) to express reliance or contingency.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses that an outcome or person relies on something using “depend”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “depend” is followed by “on” (or “upon”); “depend of” is absent.

l1_note.es: «Depender de» empuja a decir «depend of».

explanation.es: Se dice «depend on», nunca «depend of».
explanation.en: Say “depend on”, never “depend of”.

knowledge_units.name: Second conditional: past tense in if-clause
knowledge_units.behavior: In an if-clause expressing a hypothetical or unreal condition, use the past simple, not would/will.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner states a hypothetical or counterfactual condition with “if”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The verb in the if-clause is in the past simple (e.g. had, were, approved), not would or will.

l1_note.es: El subjuntivo «si tuviera» empuja a decir erróneamente «if I would have».

explanation.es: Tras «if» hipotético se usa pasado simple: «If we had more budget, we would expand».
explanation.en: In a hypothetical if-clause use the past simple: «If we had more budget, we would expand».

knowledge_units.name: “be used to + -ing” (accustomed to)
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “be used to + -ing/noun” to express being accustomed to something, and “used to + base verb” for past habits.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses familiarity or being accustomed to a routine or state in the present.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “be used to” is followed by an -ing gerund or noun phrase, not a base infinitive.
out_of_scope: used to + base verb meaning past habit

l1_note.es: «Estar acostumbrado a hacer» se confunde con «solía hacer», produciendo «I am used to work» en vez de «working».

explanation.es: Estar acostumbrado: «be used to + -ing» (I am used to working late). Pasado: «used to + verbo base».
explanation.en: Accustomed: «be used to + -ing» (I am used to working late). Past habit: «used to + base verb».

knowledge_units.name: “discuss” without “about”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “discuss” directly as a transitive verb taking its object without the preposition “about”.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner states that people are talking through an issue, plan or agenda using “discuss”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “discuss” is followed directly by its object noun phrase; “discuss about” is absent.

l1_note.es: «Discutir sobre algo» o «hablar de» invita a traducir como «discuss about».

explanation.es: Se dice «discuss the proposal», nunca «discuss about».
explanation.en: Say «discuss the proposal», never «discuss about».

knowledge_units.name: “look forward to + -ing”
knowledge_units.behavior: Follow “look forward to” with a gerund (-ing) or noun phrase, not a base verb.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner communicates positive anticipation in formal or business correspondence using “look forward to”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “look forward to” is followed by -ing (e.g. hearing, meeting); base infinitive is absent.
out_of_scope: look forward to + noun (which is also correct)

l1_note.es: «to» se confunde con la marca de infinitivo, produciendo «look forward to meet you».

explanation.es: Aquí «to» es preposición, por lo que exige gerundio: «look forward to meeting you».
explanation.en: Here «to» is a preposition, requiring -ing: «look forward to meeting you».

knowledge_units.name: “borrow” (take) vs “lend” (give)
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “borrow (from)” to receive something temporarily, and “lend (to)” to give something temporarily.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses requesting temporary use or providing temporary use of an item or capital.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “borrow” is used for receiving/taking; “lend” for giving/providing.

l1_note.es: En español «prestar» cubre ambos sentidos («¿me prestas?» y «te presto»).

explanation.es: borrow = tomar prestado («Can I borrow your badge?»). lend = prestar a otro («Can you lend me your badge?»).
explanation.en: borrow = receive temporarily («Can I borrow your badge?»). lend = give temporarily («Can you lend me your badge?»).

knowledge_units.name: “tell + person” vs “say”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “tell” with a direct personal object (tell someone), and “say” when no personal object immediately follows without “to”.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner reports speech or instructions addressed to a person.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “tell” takes a direct personal object; “say” does not take a bare personal pronoun (no “he said me”).

l1_note.es: «Él me dijo» empuja al calco «he said me» en vez de «he told me».

explanation.es: Se dice «he told me» o «he said that...», nunca «he said me».
explanation.en: Say «he told me» or «he said that...», never «he said me».

knowledge_units.name: Embedded questions: statement word order
knowledge_units.behavior: In embedded or indirect questions, use statement word order (subject + verb) without do/does inversion.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner asks or reports an indirect question embedded within a polite phrase or matrix clause.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The embedded question uses wh-word + subject + verb (e.g. where the room is), not inverted order.

l1_note.es: En español el orden no cambia entre preguntas directas e indirectas («¿Dónde está?» / «Dime dónde está»).

explanation.es: En preguntas indirectas el orden es de afirmación: «Could you tell me where the room is?» (no «where is the room»).
explanation.en: In indirect questions use statement order: «Could you tell me where the room is?» (not «where is the room»).

knowledge_units.name: Past Simple with finished time markers
knowledge_units.behavior: Use the Past Simple (not Present Perfect) when a specific finished time marker is stated (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020).
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner refers to an action occurring at a specific finished past time.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The verb is in the Past Simple; Present Perfect (have/has + participle) is absent with finished time markers.
out_of_scope: present perfect with unfinished time (this morning, today)

l1_note.es: En español se usa a menudo el pretérito perfecto para tiempos recientes («hoy he ido», «ayer he visto»).

explanation.es: Con marcadores de tiempo terminado (yesterday, last year, ago) se usa pasado simple: «We launched last week» (no «have launched»).
explanation.en: With finished time markers (yesterday, last year, ago) use the Past Simple: «We launched last week» (not «have launched»).

knowledge_units.name: Explicit subject “it” with “to be”
knowledge_units.behavior: Provide an explicit subject pronoun (especially dummy “it”) before verbs, avoiding subject omission.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner constructs an impersonal evaluation or states a fact with “to be” (e.g. it is necessary, it is true).
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The clause contains an explicit subject pronoun; subjectless forms like “is necessary” are absent.

l1_note.es: El español es una lengua pro-drop («es importante»); el inglés exige sujeto explícito («it is important»).

explanation.es: En inglés el verbo siempre necesita sujeto explícito: «It is important», nunca «Is important».
explanation.en: In English verbs require an explicit subject: «It is important», never «Is important».

knowledge_units.name: Auxiliaries “do/does” in present negatives & questions
knowledge_units.behavior: Use do/does + not and do/does + subject with the base form of the main verb, without double marking.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner negates or questions a non-be verb in the present simple.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Negations use don't/doesn't + base verb; questions invert do/does with subject.

l1_note.es: El español solo antepone «no» al verbo («él no trabaja»); en inglés se requiere auxiliar («he doesn't work»).

explanation.es: En presente se niega con don't/doesn't + verbo base: «He doesn't work», no «He not works» ni «doesn't works».
explanation.en: Present negatives require don't/doesn't + base verb: «He doesn't work», not «He not works».

knowledge_units.name: Indefinite article “a/an” with professions
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “a” or “an” before singular countable professions and roles.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner states someone's job, title or professional role.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: A singular profession is preceded by “a” or “an”; bare professions like “I am engineer” are absent.

l1_note.es: En español no se usa artículo con profesiones («soy gerente»); en inglés es obligatorio («I am a manager»).

explanation.es: Las profesiones en singular llevan «a/an»: «She is a director», «I am an architect».
explanation.en: Singular professions take «a/an»: «She is a director», «I am an architect».

knowledge_units.name: Prepositions of time: at / on / in
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “at” for clock times/exact points, “on” for days/dates, and “in” for months/years/periods.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner specifies a time coordinate in a schedule or calendar.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Clock times take “at”; days take “on”; months/years take “in”.

l1_note.es: El español usa «en» para todo («en lunes, en las 9, en julio»); el inglés distingue at/on/in.

explanation.es: Horas: «at 9:00». Días: «on Monday». Meses/años: «in September».
explanation.en: Clock times: «at 9:00». Days: «on Monday». Months/years: «in September».

knowledge_units.name: Past Simple affirmative high-frequency forms
knowledge_units.behavior: Produce correct past simple affirmative forms for high-frequency regular (-ed) and irregular verbs.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner reports completed past events or actions in the affirmative.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The verb is correctly inflected in the past simple (e.g. went, saw, met, completed).

l1_note.es: Confusión entre infinitivo y pasado, o regularizaciones incorrectas como «goed» o «seed».

explanation.es: Usa la forma de pasado simple: «We met the client», «They went to the branch».
explanation.en: Use the past simple form: «We met the client», «They went to the branch».

knowledge_units.name: Past auxiliary “didn't” + base verb
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “didn't” followed by the base form of the verb, avoiding double past marking.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner negates an action in the past simple.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “didn't” is followed by the base verb (e.g. didn't go, didn't see); forms like “didn't went” are absent.

l1_note.es: Doble marcación de pasado en el verbo principal: «didn't went» o «didn't had».

explanation.es: Con el auxiliar «didn't» el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base: «We didn't go», nunca «didn't went».
explanation.en: With the auxiliary «didn't» the main verb is in base form: «We didn't go», never «didn't went».

knowledge_units.name: Future: “be going to” for plans vs “will” for decisions
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “be going to” for pre-arranged plans/intentions, and “will” for spontaneous decisions or promises.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner communicates an established future project or immediate commitment.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Established plans use “be going to + verb”; spontaneous commitments use “will + verb”.

l1_note.es: El hispanohablante tiende a usar «will» para todo futuro, ignorando «be going to» para planes fijados.

explanation.es: Para planes e intenciones previas se usa «be going to»: «We are going to launch in Q3».
explanation.en: For prior plans use «be going to»: «We are going to launch in Q3».

knowledge_units.name: Modals “can / could” + bare infinitive
knowledge_units.behavior: Follow modal verbs “can” and “could” directly with the base verb without “to”.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses ability, permission or possibility with can/could.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “can” or “could” is followed by the bare verb; “can to + verb” is absent.

l1_note.es: «Poder hacer algo» empuja a añadir «to»: «I can to send the file».

explanation.es: Tras «can» o «could» va el verbo base directo sin «to»: «I can send», nunca «I can to send».
explanation.en: After «can» or «could» use the bare verb without «to»: «I can send», never «I can to send».

knowledge_units.name: Comparative adjectives: -er than vs more ... than
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “-er than” for short adjectives (faster than) and “more ... than” for long adjectives (more efficient than).
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner compares two products, solutions, or metrics.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Short adjectives take “-er than”; long adjectives take “more ... than”; “more faster” is absent.

l1_note.es: «Más rápido que» provoca el calco «more fast than» o dobles formas como «more better».

explanation.es: Adjetivos cortos llevan «-er»: «faster than». Adjetivos largos llevan «more»: «more reliable than».
explanation.en: Short adjectives take «-er»: «faster than». Long adjectives take «more»: «more reliable than».

knowledge_units.name: Verb patterns: gerund vs infinitive
knowledge_units.behavior: Follow specific matrix verbs with either a gerund (avoid, enjoy) or an infinitive (decide, promise).
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner chains two verbs together (e.g. avoid making, decide to review).
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The complement matches the required verb pattern; errors like “avoid to make” are absent.

l1_note.es: En español se usa infinitivo para ambos («evitar hacer», «decidir hacer»), generando errores como «avoid to do».

explanation.es: Verbos como «avoid» o «enjoy» exigen gerundio: «avoid taking risks», «enjoy meeting clients».
explanation.en: Verbs like «avoid» or «enjoy» require a gerund: «avoid taking risks», «enjoy meeting clients».

knowledge_units.name: Preposition “listen to”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “listen to” with its object, never omitting the preposition “to”.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner expresses paying attention to audio, advice or a speaker using “listen”.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “listen” is followed by “to”; bare forms like “listen the client” are absent.

l1_note.es: «Escuchar algo / a alguien» es directo en español («escuchar la propuesta»), provocando «listen the proposal».

explanation.es: Se dice «listen to the presentation», nunca «listen the presentation».
explanation.en: Say «listen to the presentation», never «listen the presentation».

knowledge_units.name: Present Perfect Continuous for duration
knowledge_units.behavior: Use have/has been + -ing to emphasize ongoing duration or activity up to the present.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner emphasizes the ongoing duration of an activity (e.g. with for/since/all day).
knowledge_units.success_criterion: The verb phrase uses have/has been + -ing; simple present continuous like “I am working since 9am” is absent.

l1_note.es: «Llevo trabajando dos horas» empuja al error «I am working for two hours».

explanation.es: Para acciones en curso con duración se usa «have been doing»: «We have been working on this all morning».
explanation.en: For ongoing duration use «have been doing»: «We have been working on this all morning».

knowledge_units.name: Modals of deduction: must be / must have been
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “must be / can't be” for present deduction and “must have / can't have + past participle” for past deduction.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner draws a logical conclusion from evidence in the past or present.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Past deduction uses modal + have + past participle; forms like “must was” or “must be happened” are absent.

l1_note.es: «Debe haber sido» se traduce incorrectamente como «must was» o «should have been» en deducción lógica.

explanation.es: Deducción pasada: «must have been», «can't have been»: «The email must have bounced».
explanation.en: Past deduction: «must have been», «can't have been»: «The email must have bounced».

knowledge_units.name: Concession connectors: “despite + noun/-ing” vs “although + clause”
knowledge_units.behavior: Use “despite / in spite of” with a noun phrase or gerund, and “although / even though” with a full clause (subject + verb).
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner connects contrasting ideas expressing concession.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: “despite” is followed by a noun/gerund; “although” is followed by a clause; “despite + clause” is absent.

l1_note.es: «A pesar de que» empuja a decir «despite that he was...» o «despite he was...» sin «the fact that».

explanation.es: «Despite + sustantivo/-ing»: «Despite the delay». «Although + sujeto + verbo»: «Although it was delayed».
explanation.en: «Despite + noun/-ing»: «Despite the delay». «Although + subject + verb»: «Although it was delayed».

knowledge_units.name: Passive voice in continuous and perfect tenses
knowledge_units.behavior: Form the passive voice correctly in continuous (is being + participle) and perfect (has been + participle) tenses.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner describes an ongoing process or completed state where the patient is the subject.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: Continuous passives use “be + being + past participle”; perfect passives use “have/has been + past participle”.

l1_note.es: «Se está actualizando» empuja a calcos como «is updating» o «is being update».

explanation.es: Pasiva continua: «is being updated». Pasiva perfecta: «has been resolved».
explanation.en: Continuous passive: «is being updated». Perfect passive: «has been resolved».

knowledge_units.name: Third conditional: past counterfactual hypotheses
knowledge_units.behavior: In third conditional sentences, use “if + had + past participle” in the if-clause, and “would have + past participle” in the result clause.
knowledge_units.obligatory_context: The learner reflects on past unchangeable outcomes and alternative possibilities.
knowledge_units.success_criterion: If-clause uses had + past participle (not would have); result clause uses would have + past participle.

l1_note.es: «Si hubiéramos sabido» provoca el doble would: «If we would have known, we would have acted».

explanation.es: Tercer condicional: «If we had known the risk, we would have stopped the launch».
explanation.en: Third conditional: «If we had known the risk, we would have stopped the launch».

error_signatures.name: Missing -s/-es
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Con un sujeto singular de tercera persona el verbo lleva -s/-es: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. A singular third-person subject needs -s/-es: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: Wrong preposition after responsible
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Con «responsible» se usa «for»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. “Responsible” takes “for”: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: will/would inside the if-clause
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Tras «if», en una condición futura real, se usa presente: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. After “if” in a real future condition, use the present: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: “to” after make/let + object
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Después de make/let + objeto va el verbo base, sin «to»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. After make/let + object use the base verb, no “to”: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: -ing after make/let + object
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Después de make/let + objeto va el verbo base, no -ing: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. After make/let + object use the base verb, not -ing: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: Wrong word form of manage
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Aquí hace falta otra forma de la familia: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. This slot needs a different form of the family: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: “be + agree” calque
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». En inglés «agree» es un verbo directo: se dice «{correction}» (sin verbo to be).
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. In English “agree” is a verb: say “{correction}” (do not use “be”).

error_signatures.name: “since” used with duration
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Con una duración o periodo de tiempo se usa «for»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. Use “for” with a duration or length of time: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: “depend of” preposition calque
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». El verbo «depend» se acompaña de «on»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. “Depend” takes “on”: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: would/will in hypothetical if-clause
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». En una condición hipotética con «if», el verbo va en pasado simple: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. In a hypothetical if-clause, use the past simple: «{correction}».

error_signatures.name: base infinitive after be used to
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Para expresar estar acostumbrado, se usa «be used to + -ing»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. To express being accustomed, use “be used to + -ing”: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: “about” after discuss
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». El verbo «discuss» es directo y no lleva «about»: «{correction}».
error_signatures.feedback_en: You wrote “{quote}”. “Discuss” takes a direct object without “about”: “{correction}”.

error_signatures.name: base verb after look forward to
error_signatures.feedback_es: Escribiste «{quote}». Tras «look forward to» va un gerundio (-ing): «{correction}».

exercises.prompt: Soy gerente de operaciones en una empresa de tecnología.
accepted: I am an operations manager at a technology company.
I'm an operations manager at a technology company.

exercises.prompt: We are looking for ___ senior backend engineer with Go experience.
accepted: a

exercises.prompt: Rewrite stating his role: David works in financial auditing as a professional.
accepted: David is a financial auditor.
David is an auditor.

exercises.prompt: Ella es abogada corporativa y representa al inversor principal.
accepted: She is a corporate lawyer and represents the lead investor.
She's a corporate lawyer and represents the lead investor.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with your professional title: “Before founding this startup, she was …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'a/an + profession' (e.g. 'a software architect', 'an executive director'). Omission of article is a violation.

exercises.prompt: The budget review starts ___ 10:30 AM tomorrow. (at/on/in)
accepted: at

exercises.prompt: Presentaremos la propuesta el próximo lunes.
accepted: We will present the proposal on Monday.
We'll present the proposal on Monday.
We will present the proposal next Monday.

exercises.prompt: The next major platform release is scheduled ___ November. (at/on/in)
accepted: in

exercises.prompt: Rewrite specifying the exact day: The summit occurs in May, specifically May 15th.
accepted: The summit occurs on May 15th.
The summit takes place on May 15th.

exercises.prompt: El contrato finaliza a finales de año, en 2027.
accepted: The contract ends at the end of the year, in 2027.
The contract expires at the end of the year, in 2027.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with an exact time: “Our flight to London lands …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'at + time' (e.g. 'at 4:00 PM'). 'in' or 'on' with clock time is a violation.

exercises.prompt: Our regional team ___ (exceed) the revenue forecast last quarter.
accepted: exceeded

exercises.prompt: Nos reunimos con el cliente y vimos la demostración.
accepted: We met with the client and saw the demonstration.
We met the client and saw the demo.

exercises.prompt: The automated monitor ___ (send) an alert as soon as latency spiked.
accepted: sent

exercises.prompt: Change to past simple: The founders write the initial business plan.
accepted: The founders wrote the initial business plan.

exercises.prompt: Ellos aceptaron nuestra oferta y firmaron el acuerdo ayer.
accepted: They accepted our offer and signed the agreement yesterday.
They accepted our offer and signed the deal yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with past actions: “Last week our engineering squad …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for correct past simple regular/irregular forms (e.g. 'completed the sprint', 'built the prototype'). Base forms are a violation.

exercises.prompt: The accounting division did not ___ (notice) the discrepancy until yesterday.
accepted: notice

exercises.prompt: Nosotros no vimos ningún error en los registros del servidor.
accepted: We did not see any errors in the server logs.
We didn't see any errors in the server logs.

exercises.prompt: Why didn't the vendor ___ (send) the revised scope of work?
accepted: send

exercises.prompt: Make negative using “didn't”: The executive team approved the merger last year.
accepted: The executive team didn't approve the merger last year.
The executive team did not approve the merger last year.

exercises.prompt: El cliente no vino a la presentación final.
accepted: The client did not come to the final presentation.
The client didn't come to the final presentation.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with a negative past action: “During the international workshop, we didn't …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'didn't + base verb' (e.g. 'didn't incur extra expenses', 'didn't rent a car'). Inflected past verb is a violation.

exercises.situation: Stating an established Q4 strategic roadmap.
exercises.prompt: We have secured the budget, so we are ___ (go) to hire five software architects.
accepted: going

exercises.prompt: Vamos a migrar los servidores este fin de semana.
accepted: We are going to migrate the servers this weekend.
We're going to migrate the servers this weekend.

exercises.situation: Spontaneous offer during a conference call.
exercises.prompt: Don't worry about the minutes; I ___ send them to everyone after the call. (will/am going to)
accepted: will

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “going to”: The company has decided to launch operations in Mexico next month.
accepted: The company is going to launch operations in Mexico next month.

exercises.situation: Spontaneous agreement in a deal room.
exercises.prompt: Trato hecho; te llamaré mañana por la mañana.
accepted: Deal; I will call you tomorrow morning.
Deal; I'll call you tomorrow morning.

known_wrong.text: i am going to call you

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with an approved plan: “In accordance with board approval, we are going to …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'be going to + base verb' expressing pre-arranged strategic plan.

exercises.prompt: The new API can ___ (process) ten thousand concurrent requests.
accepted: process

exercises.situation: Offering assistance to a project manager.
exercises.prompt: Puedo enviar el informe financiero esta tarde.
accepted: I can send the financial report this afternoon.

exercises.situation: Polite inquiry to an enterprise supplier.
exercises.prompt: Could you please ___ (provide) the updated price list?
accepted: provide

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “can”: You have permission to approve travel budgets under five thousand dollars.
accepted: You can approve travel budgets under five thousand dollars.

exercises.prompt: No podemos aceptar esas condiciones de pago.
accepted: We cannot accept those payment terms.
We can't accept those payment terms.
We cannot accept those payment conditions.

exercises.situation: Highlighting system benefits in a client demo.
exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence: “With our machine learning pipeline, your analysts can …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for bare verb after can (e.g. 'can detect anomalies faster'). 'can to + verb' is a target violation.

exercises.prompt: The new indexing strategy is ___ (fast) than the previous query planner.
accepted: faster

exercises.prompt: Esta solución es más eficiente que la alternativa existente.
accepted: This solution is more efficient than the existing alternative.
This solution is more efficient than the current alternative.

exercises.prompt: Their revised price point is ___ (low) than our initial target.
accepted: lower

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “better than”: The new workflow exceeds the old system in quality.
accepted: The new workflow is better than the old system.

exercises.prompt: Nuestra plataforma es más segura que la de la competencia.
accepted: Our platform is more secure than the competition's.
Our platform is more secure than our competitors'.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence comparing sprints: “With continuous integration, deployment is now …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for correct comparative (e.g. 'faster than before', 'more reliable than last quarter'). 'more fast' is a target violation.

exercises.prompt: We must avoid ___ (take) uncalculated compliance risks in this market.
accepted: taking

exercises.prompt: El comité decidió posponer el lanzamiento de la función.
accepted: The committee decided to postpone the feature launch.
The committee decided to delay the feature launch.

exercises.prompt: Our partners enjoy ___ (work) with our customer success team.
accepted: working

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “agreed to”: Both parties gave consent to share the audit report.
accepted: Both parties agreed to share the audit report.

exercises.prompt: Sugerimos migrar los microservicios gradualmente.
accepted: We suggest migrating the microservices gradually.
We suggested migrating the microservices gradually.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with an -ing complement: “To prevent security incidents, we strictly avoid …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for gerund after avoid (e.g. 'storing credentials in plain text'). 'to store' is a target violation.

exercises.prompt: We need to listen ___ the stakeholders before finalizing the roadmap. (to/of/at)
accepted: to

exercises.prompt: Un buen líder siempre escucha a su equipo.
accepted: A good leader always listens to their team.
A good leader always listens to his team.
A good leader always listens to her team.

exercises.prompt: The procurement director listened ___ our explanation with great attention.
accepted: to

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “listen to”: We pay close attention to user feedback.
accepted: We listen to user feedback.

exercises.prompt: El público escuchó atentamente la presentación del producto.
accepted: The audience listened to the product presentation attentively.
The audience listened attentively to the product presentation.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence: “If the engineering leads had listened …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'listened to + object' (e.g. 'listened to the warnings', 'listened to the QA report'). Omission of 'to' is a violation.

exercises.prompt: Our DevOps squad has ___ (investigate) the latency spike since 8 AM.
accepted: been investigating

exercises.prompt: Llevamos colaborando con este proveedor durante tres años.
accepted: We have been collaborating with this supplier for three years.
We've been collaborating with this supplier for three years.

known_wrong.text: we are collaborating with this supplier for three years

exercises.prompt: She has ___ (lead) the transformation team since last November.
accepted: been leading

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “have been working”: We started working on this patch three days ago and are still doing it.
accepted: We have been working on this patch for three days.
We've been working on this patch for three days.

known_wrong.text: we are working on this patch for three days

exercises.prompt: El equipo ha estado probando el software toda la semana.
accepted: The team has been testing the software all week.
The team have been testing the software all week.

known_wrong.text: team is testing the software all week

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with an ongoing duration: “Both legal teams have been …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for have been + -ing (e.g. 'have been reviewing the clauses for weeks'). Simple continuous is a target violation.

exercises.situation: Root cause deduction after a service crash.
exercises.prompt: The primary cluster was offline; the backup service must have ___ (take) over automatically.
accepted: taken

exercises.prompt: El correo debe de haber ido a la carpeta de spam.
accepted: The email must have gone to the spam folder.
The message must have gone to the spam folder.

exercises.prompt: With ten thousand pre-orders, the product launch ___ be a commercial success. (must/can't)
accepted: must

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using “must have”: I am virtually certain that the CEO approved the budget increase.
accepted: The CEO must have approved the budget increase.

exercises.prompt: Ellos no pueden haber firmado con otro proveedor tan rápido.
accepted: They can't have signed with another supplier so quickly.
They cannot have signed with another supplier so quickly.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with past deduction: “The vendor didn't join the call, so they must have …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'must have + past participle' (e.g. 'must have forgotten the time'). 'must forget' or 'must forgot' is a target violation.

exercises.prompt: ___ the supply chain disruptions, Q3 operating margins reached 24%. (Despite/Although)
accepted: Despite

exercises.prompt: A pesar de que el plazo era ajustado, entregamos la función sin errores.
accepted: Although the deadline was tight, we delivered the feature without bugs.
Although the deadline was tight, we delivered the feature without errors.
Even though the deadline was tight, we delivered the feature without bugs.

exercises.prompt: ___ the market was volatile, the board reaffirmed its expansion strategy. (Although/Despite)
accepted: Although

exercises.prompt: Rewrite starting with “Despite”: Although there were several technical delays, the pilot succeeded.
accepted: Despite several technical delays, the pilot succeeded.

known_wrong.text: despite there were several technical delays

exercises.prompt: A pesar del incremento de costes, mantuvimos el precio acordado.
accepted: Despite the increase in costs, we maintained the agreed price.
Despite rising costs, we maintained the agreed price.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with a noun phrase: “Our customer retention remained strong despite …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for noun phrase or gerund after despite (e.g. 'despite market turbulence'). A full clause (subject + verb) without 'the fact that' is a violation.

exercises.prompt: The core authentication microservice is currently being ___ (upgrade).
accepted: upgraded

exercises.prompt: El problema de seguridad ha sido resuelto por los ingenieros.
accepted: The security issue has been resolved by the engineers.
The security bug has been resolved by the engineers.

exercises.prompt: All vendor invoices have ___ (process) by accounts payable.
accepted: been processed

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in passive continuous: The legal team is reviewing the new policy right now.
accepted: The new policy is being reviewed by the legal team right now.
The new policy is being reviewed right now.

exercises.prompt: Los servidores están siendo configurados en este momento.
accepted: The servers are being configured right now.
The servers are being configured at the moment.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with present perfect passive: “The revised clauses have …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'have been + past participle' (e.g. 'have been approved by legal'). Active verb form or missing 'been' is a violation.

exercises.prompt: If we had ___ (conduct) due diligence earlier, we would have avoided the liability.
accepted: conducted

exercises.prompt: Si hubiéramos detectado el fallo antes, habríamos prevenido la caída del sistema.
accepted: If we had detected the bug earlier, we would have prevented the system outage.
If we had detected the bug earlier, we'd have prevented the system outage.
If we had detected the failure earlier, we would have prevented the outage.

exercises.prompt: If the executive board ___ (approve) the budget, we would have launched the platform in June.
accepted: had approved

exercises.situation: Reflecting on a missed client deadline.
exercises.prompt: Rewrite as third conditional starting with “If the client had”: The client did not send the specs, so we missed the release date.
accepted: If the client had sent the specs, we would have met the release date.
If the client had sent the specs, we wouldn't have missed the release date.

known_wrong.text: if the client would have sent

exercises.prompt: Habríamos firmado el contrato si ellos hubieran rebajado el precio.
accepted: We would have signed the contract if they had lowered the price.
We'd have signed the contract if they had lowered the price.

exercises.prompt: Finish the sentence with a counterfactual past consequence: “If the team had received the API keys in time, we …”
exercises.notes_for_evaluator: Check for 'would have + past participle' (e.g. 'would have completed the integration'). 'would complete' or 'had completed' in result clause is a violation.
